newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. appoints new Orange County supervisor.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. appoints new Orange County supervisor.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson on Wednesday appointed Thomas Wilson to the Orange County, Calif., Board of Supervisors.

"Tom's broad local government experience and background as a manager in the private sector makes him uniquely suited to step in and face the diverse challenges of Orange County's Fifth Supervisorial District," Gov. Wilson said in a statement announcing the appointment.
Board members receive a salary of just over $82,000 a year. The appointment does not require state Senate confirmation.
Thomas Wilson assumes the seat of Marian Bergeson, who quit earlier this year to become Gov. Wilson's top education advisor.

Thomas Wilson, 56, currently serves as a member of the Laguna Niguel City Council, where he has served since 1989. During his tenure on the city council, he served two terms as major pro tempore and was elected mayor for a two-year term.

Thomas Wilson is also currently chairman of the Orange County Fire Authority, a member of the board of directors for the Orange County Transportation Authority and a member of the executive steering committee of the Orange County chapter of the League of Cities.

Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the federal Bankruptcy Code on December 6, 1994, after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion. The county emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year.
